plug._comment: 12-point model, per user's real caliper measurements of the physical SFP plug. Depth (insertion axis): a1-a4 = 0in (near/tip face), a5-a8 = 0.75in = 19.05mm, a9-a12 = 1.5in = 38.10mm (visible reference line, not the physical end of the part). Cross-section: a1-a4 (thickness, y-axis) = 0.275in = 6.985mm full (half=3.4925mm) -- corrected from an initial 0.225in reading after a real single-camera reprojection check (frame_001, calibration/camera-identity/depth all independently verified correct first) showed 0.275in roughly HALVES the per-point fit residual on both left (6.74px->4.29px mean) and right (8.03px->4.06px mean), computed with zero cross-camera math involved, isolating this as a genuine geometry correction rather than click-noise or a calibration artifact. a3-a4 (width, x-axis) = 0.5in = 12.7mm full (half=6.35mm), confirmed correct. Residual 4-6px per-point error remains even after this fix, concentrated on the a9-a12 far points -- still not fully explained, may indicate a9-a12 aren't exactly on the same x,y as a1-a4 (real housing taper/step at that depth) rather than a further cross-section correction. The -0.0020 tip-face z-inset is a stability margin carried over from the sim model, not part of the measured depth.

8-point TAPERED cuboid -- rear face is physically larger than the near face, confirmed by real caliper measurement (2026-09-17): near face (c1,c2,c3,c4) is 0.8in x 0.3in (width x height), rear face (c5,c6,c7,c8) is 1.0in x 0.5in. Depth (near to rear, insertion axis) = 0.5in = 12.7mm, unchanged from an earlier round. Near-face tip inset (-0.00265) unchanged, a stability margin not part of any measured dimension. IMPORTANT: because the two faces are different sizes, a 'side face' (e.g. c1,c5,c8,c4) is NOT a parallelogram -- verified false (c1+c8 != c5+c4) before this was caught. Only the near-face rectangle [c1,c2,c3,c4] is still a valid same-plane parallelogram (kept in 'rectangles' below); the rear-face corners are filled instead via compute_affine_completion (fits one 2-D affine map from ALL known local-3D points to their pixels, then predicts the rest -- correct for any known rigid shape, taper included, not just parallelograms). Left's reference set (c1,c3,c4,c5,c6) and right's (c1,c2,c4,c5,c6) each have >=4 non-coplanar known points once the near-face rectangle fills in, satisfying compute_affine_completion's requirement.
